_words: Every number of the slate-in-layers work (layers inside one Blender recipe, pure procedural, not fitted). Same-kind = lib/texture_compare.py against the slate reference (a guide only); dot-for-dot = lib/pixel_compare.py, for transparency only. Written by integration/takeover/make_final_report.py from the result files.
who: five layer builders; first integrator (tuning rounds 1-13, most bakes; cut off by a machine restart at about 03:15 on 20 October); second integrator (checked everything, re-ran what was cut off, wrote the guides and this report)

edits to layer files during integration.change: new control `mottle_tallness` (socket `Mottle Tallness`, default 2.2 = the old fixed value, range 0.5 to 6)
edits to layer files during integration.why: the flat patches inside a slate ran the whole slate height, so slates looked like corrugated sheets of stripes; the reference has strokes that stop part way. Default is unchanged so nothing else moves.

edits to layer files during integration.change: new control `tone_blend` (socket `Tone Blend`, default 0 = old behaviour, range 0 to 1): mixes the real relief with a height made from the finished colour's brightness (the reference's own formula, 2.5 x (brightness - 9.5))
edits to layer files during integration.why: the reference height maps were made from the colour, ours is real relief (chips sunk); the "same kind" height measures reward the colour-made height. One honest knob lets a person choose.

tuning rounds measured before their pict._words: Numbers measured by the second integrator on the previous integrator's look pictures just before those pictures were deleted to stay under the 400 MB limit (colour group = lib/texture_compare.py 'same kind' colour group against the slate reference; difference = against outputs/default/colour.png, same seeds, 1254 dots).
tuning rounds measured before their pict.note on score_set.py: its normal_height_agreement comes out 0.0 for all three (as first written; only the 0.7 bake was checked again). The harness's own normal, which score_set.py also makes, gives 0.0 for the 0.7 bake; the strength-7 normal of integration/make_normal.py gives 0.534 for it. So the normal group by score_set.py is lower than the strength-7 group (0.604 against 0.671 for the 0.7 bake); the height group does not depend on it. (Corrected after the second honesty check: this note first had the two normal maps the wrong way round: it said the harness's own normal gives 0.534.)

tuning round 14 (second integrator; resu._words: Tuning round 14, by the second integrator after the restart. Prompted by the whole-recipe strips (768 dots), where a lighter shadow (shadow_darkness 0 or 0.3) and stronger streaks (streak_contrast 2.1) raised the colour group most. All pictures 1254 dots, colour group of lib/texture_compare.py against the slate reference. 'default seeds' = the seeds of the default tile; seeds_b = layout 101, colour 111, damage 121, moss 131, outline 141; seeds_c = 202, 212, 222, 232, 242.
tuning round 14 (second integrator; resu.what most of the gain was: the colour_scale measure (the 'feature size' cliff): default seeds 0.452 -> 0.922 for r14d; on seeds_b 0.845 -> 0.918 and seeds_c 0.85 -> 0.853. Colour distribution, orientation and gradient went slightly DOWN with r14d.
tuning round 14 (second integrator; resu.decision: kept the first integrator's settings: the default seeds are the unlucky ones (0.701, the lowest of five seed sets of the default settings: 0.701, 0.765, 0.769, 0.753, 0.710), and r14d gains only 0.005 to 0.011 on the other seeds, less than the seed spread. The look of r14d (a lighter shadow band, more contrasted streaks) is at least as close to the reference by eye, so it is offered as a setting choice, not adopted (adopting it would have meant re-baking every result in the folder for a gain smaller than the seed noise).

look fixes (round 15)._words: Look fixes (round 15, 20 October): a look checker listed 11 faults of the default tile, a tuner fixed them by hand in two rounds (settings 49 to 73, six new controls in two layer files), the look checker looked again, and a re-baker made again everything that depends on the default settings. Every number below is for the NEW default unless it says "before". The old numbers above in this file are the OLD default and are kept.

settings file.note: the other 182 - 73 = 109 controls keep the layer files starting values; the whole description is about 6 KB (checked for the first 176 only)

new controls (the only code changes): layers/moss.py (round 2): four new controls, all defaulting to the old picture: rim_opacity and core_opacity (see-through moss paint: opacity runs from the rim value at the edge of a clump to the core value inside it; only the mask is see-through, height and roughness unchanged), side_clearance (moss growth fades out near side joints, 0 = off) and fleck_amount (scales the small light and dark flecks, 1 = as before).
layers/outline_and_shadow.py (round 2): two new controls: joint_texture (faint fine mottling of the joint black, 0 = flat as before) and joint_texture_size (mottles per tile, default 600).

Old copies of both files: look_fixes/round2/layer_files_before_round2/. All six new controls are listed in integration/CHANGES_TO_LAYER_FILES.md (rows 3 to 6). recipe/controls.md was rebuilt with recipe/make_controls_table.py.

Tests of the code changes: (1) the settings of the end of round 1 baked at 384 dots with the old and the new files give identical colour, height and roughness (largest difference 0); (2) independence re-run for moss and outline_and_shadow (Amount 0 and Seed + 1 each, new default settings, 384 dots): 0.0 % of dots changed outside the changed layer's own region, no other layer's mask changed (look_fixes/round2/independence/independence_two_layers_table.md, also in the changes file). Not re-run: half-tile shift test; independence of unchanged layers.

recipe/settings.json: 65 -> 73 entries; net 46 entries differ from the start of round 1 (settings_before_look_fixes.json, 49 entries). Settings of round 2 alone: look_fixes/round2/set_F_round2_all_changes.json; the end of round 1: look_fixes/round2/settings_after_round1.json.

outputs/default/ re-baked at 1254 dots (colour, 16-bit height, roughness, metallic, harness normal renamed normal_harness_sobel.png, normal_bumpnode.png, and normal.png = strength-7 normal from integration/make_normal.py); score_same_kind.json, score_pixel_for_transparency.json, sheet_same_kind.jpg and log.txt rewritten. outputs/default_before_look_fixes and recipe/settings_before_look_fixes.json untouched.

New tools in look_fixes/: independence_two_layers_bake.py and independence_two_layers_analysis.py; round2/independent_measures.py (copy of the checker's own measuring script, with command-line pictures and its own json output), round2/moss_character.py, round2/run_facets_and_independence.py, round2/run_lit_and_variations.py; bake_variants.py now accepts a per-variant size.
Round 1 pictures and scores kept in look_fixes/round_1_pictures/.

problems status.problem: 1 Paint handling (liquified flame tongues, wavy rippled edges)
problems status.evidence: Ripple is gone and the paint is now broad flat bands with crisp edges and the fine grain is back (crop_paint_1to1.jpg, crop_paint_2x.jpg, crop_lower_edge_3x.jpg). Tuner-rule numbers re-run at 1254 dots: median grey slope inside slates 3.06 -> 1.91 (reference 1.86); hard-edge share 28.4 % -> 23.8 % (reference 15.1 %); side-to-side over up-down slope 2.44 -> 2.08 (reference 1.61); grain noise 1.0 (reference 1.0); inner spread of a slate 11.7 -> 11.2 (reference 12.3). Not fixed: tongues are still pointed flames, the paint is still more upright-stripy than the reference, and the broader cells brought a NEW fault, straight-edged flat facets (see new problems).

problems status.problem: 2 Moss (too much, flat khaki stain, rows of teeth)
problems status.evidence: Teeth and flakes are gone; the moss is now a soft see-through olive wash with the slate streaks showing through, hanging from the top edges (crop_moss_2x.jpg, crop_moss_b_2x.jpg, crop_side_joint_moss.jpg). Mine (Lab rule): moss share of slate dots 13.6 % -> 6.5 % (reference 9.0 %); largest moss slate 81 % -> 52 % (reference 26 %); moss in the top third of the slate 49 % -> 42 % (reference 32 %). Tuner rule: moss pieces over 1500 dots 31 -> 13 (reference 13), share of moss in big pieces 71.6 % -> 51.0 % (reference 52.8 %). It has overshot a little to the pale side: dots with b* above 8 (strong olive) 9.1 % -> 2.3 % (reference 5.0 %); slates with over 5 % moss 60 % -> 32 % (reference 67 %, my rule). Reads as dull brownish-olive with a combed vertical texture rather than the reference's yellower mottled patches.

problems status.problem: 3 Chips and damage (big tan L-shapes at the lower corners)
problems status.evidence: L-shapes at the corners are gone (full_after.jpg, compare_full_reference_before_after.jpg, crop_lower_edge2_3x.jpg). Tuner rule: tan share 2.23 % -> 1.47 % (reference 1.56 %); tan in pieces of 300+ dots 52.9 % -> 25.2 % (reference 35.6 %); round tan dots 39 -> 24 (reference 28). Mine (Lab, cream/tan/pink dots): chip share of tile 0.82 % -> 0.37 % (reference 0.17 %); chip area in chunky pieces (width 7+ dots) 73 % -> 41 % (reference 45 %); chip-coloured share of the lower rim 4.1 % -> 1.4 % (reference 0.9 %). Left over: along most slates the chips are still a thin ragged fringe, not chunky cream flakes; a few places (x 560-760, y 200-230) look right.

Lower corners are clearly rounded now and the lower edges are more uneven (tiled3x3_after_corner_1to1.jpg, crop_lower_edge_3x.jpg). Mine: corner rise 7.4 -> 15.8 dots (reference 21.3); lower-edge mid-scale wobble 1.04 -> 1.63 (reference 2.78); row band wander 2.54 -> 3.32 dots (reference 4.13). Tuner rule: corner rise 6.8 -> 14.8 (reference 17.7); wobble 1.33 -> 2.21 (reference 2.98). About three quarters of the way to the reference; rows are still straighter than the reference. The new rounded corners leave a black wedge where an upright joint meets the row band (crop_side_joint_moss_b.jpg).

new problems: MAJOR, NEW: straight-edged flat paint facets (a low-poly, cut-glass look). About 14 slates carry a flat dark or pale polygon with straight slanting edges that is visible at normal contrast at 1:1 (marked 1-10 in facets_marked_on_contrast_boosted_after.jpg; for example x480-775,y75-225; the dark rectangle x985-1065,y80-195; the dark triangles x375-455,y560-655 and x810-895,y575-695). The BEFORE tile has none and the reference has none. They show as straight scratches under the raking light (lit_zoom_side_by_side.jpg) and as repeated arrowhead shapes in the 3x3 tiling. They came in with the broader, taller paint cells (streak_width 0.014 -> 0.03, mottle_tallness 1.1 -> 1.5) once the edge wobble was turned down. The tuner admitted this and could not remove it with settings. My automatic facet finders (line segments, edge directions, flat-patch outlines) all failed, so the count is by eye (my_straight_edges.py records the failure). This is the most noticeable difference from the reference now.

The lower rim reads as frayed or chewed: a thin pale-grey lip with a pink-orange fringe and dark speckles, instead of the reference's smooth pale line with a few chunky cream chips (crop_lower_edge_3x.jpg, crop_lower_edge2_3x.jpg). By number the rim is as busy as the reference (column-to-column lightness step 2.54 against 2.36 reference, 1.75 before; mid-scale wobble still lower, 1.63 against 2.78), so it is a difference of character, not amount. Visible at 1:1 on every slate.

Moss has gone slightly too pale and too widespread-thin: strong olive dots 2.3 % against 5.0 % in the reference (9.1 % before), moss on over 1 % of slates in 67 % against 94 % (my rule); at the 3x3 scale the tile looks bluer and less olive than the reference (tiled3x3_after.jpg against tiled3x3_reference.jpg). Less serious than the old over-mossing. The tuner's own olive-share rule under-counts see-through moss, as the tuner said.
Relief is still weaker than the reference (mean tilt 20.2 against 23.7) and different in character: thin scratches and straight facet lines instead of chunky pitted chips.

Repeat landmarks in 3x3: the pair of grey-brown flat slates in the row near y 940 (and a third at x643,y780), the dark mossy brown slate at x560-720,y1030-1160, the dark rectangle slate at x985-1065,y80-195, and the facet triangles. No seams: wrap-round difference at the tile edge is 1.01 (colour), 1.03 (normal) and 1.03 (height) times the difference between inside neighbours, left-right; up-down the wrap is smaller than inside because both edges are dark joint rows. 3x3 looked at in tiled3x3_after.jpg and tiled3x3_after_corner_1to1.jpg.

Small: whole tile a little darker (slate-face lightness L 26.4 against 27.8 in the reference; mean L 23.7 against 25.2 by the tuner; dark dots 12.9 % against 11.3 %); slightly bluer slate faces (b* -1.36 against -1.12). Not visible side by side.
Small: a pale hairline at x1175-1210,y660 is left over; black wedge flares where an upright joint meets the row band at the rounded corners.

Checked and NOT a problem: slates are not too plain (inner spread 11.2 against 12.3, plain slates 3 of 59 against 1 of 45), the paint is not blurry (grain noise 1.0 as in the reference, hard-edge share 23.8 % against 15.1 %), chips are visible, the relief is not exaggerated (weaker, not stronger), and there are no tiling seams.
look checker second look (round 2).overall: Better than before on 10 of the 11 problems, but not yet the same hand. FIXED: chips at the corners (3), shadow band (6), lone crack (8), lichen dots (9), moss cut at side joints (11). BETTER: paint ripple (1), moss amount and softness (2), slate shape (4), relief character (5), outlier slates (7). SAME: variations (10, not attempted). Nothing got worse than before on the 11 problems, but the round introduced one new major fault: about 14 slates carry flat straight-edged polygon facets that neither the BEFORE tile nor the reference has; this is now the first thing an art director would point at, and it also shows as straight scratches in the raking-light render. Next come the frayed, pink-fringed lower rim (a difference of character), relief that is still weaker and thinner than the reference, and a few remaining pale or dark outlier slates that repeat as landmarks when tiled. The tuner's claims hold in direction: I re-ran its numbers and they match (paint slope 1.91, side joints 7.2 %, tan 1.47 %, corner rise 14.8). My own cross-checks agree on direction but show less perfect values: slate-to-slate spread 6.9 against 5.1 reference (tuner's rule says 5.57 against 5.51), moss near side joints 5.0 % against 5.8 % (agrees), far-off slates 6 of 60 (tuner's rule says 2 of 59). Tiling is clean. Would an art director accept it as the same hand? Nearly: same material, same palette, same row layout and same kind of hand-painted dry-brush, but the cut-glass facets and the frayed rim give it away within a few seconds at 1:1.
